blindSummary:
The day-to-day risk here is small for a transgender visitor, with exposure concentrated in two specific situations. If you are arrested for any reason, including a protest or minor offence, a trans woman is likely to be placed in a men's prison on the basis of her legal gender — a systemic practice documented with foreign trans women subjected to genital-exam "verification," isolation and abuse. The country's own detention watchdog says trans detainees "suffer the most," and a 2025 case (a trans woman arrested in motorway-construction protests, held in a men's prison in isolation) drew parliamentary censure.

At the border, trans women — especially travellers who are racialised or read as foreign — have been humiliated by border police (a documented case at the country's main international airport), and airport waiting-zones draw repeated discrimination criticism.

Offsetting this: there is no restriction on bathroom use, and the social norm leans trans-inclusive (a hostel in a large provincial city in 2024 sanctioned a guest who complained about a trans person in a female dorm as "transphobic"). Anti-discrimination and hate-crime law cover gender identity. The risk is harassment-level in day-to-day tourism, with the serious-but-rare arrest/placement axis being the main caveat.
blindOutOfScope: Urban crime (pickpocketing, theft) in the capital and other large cities, and the general risk of civil unrest/protests, affect all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: News outlet feature (Jan 2018): trans women incarcerated in this country on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area and are punished beyond their alleged crimes - placement problems in the prison system.

The national detention watchdog's opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: based on ~40 referrals since 2010, finds serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all places of detention; recommendations also apply to intersex and non-binary persons.

Anti-torture organisation blog: interview with the national preventive-mechanism body on its 2021 opinion - trans persons deprived of liberty face constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; a new opinion was needed because the 2010 opinion had not resolved the problems.
Daily news site (Feb 2025): why a trans woman arrested in motorway-construction protests was detained in a men's prison - illustrates ongoing placement problems for trans women in custody here.
Parliamentary oral question on the condition of transgender women - parliamentary scrutiny of the treatment of trans women (including in detention).

First-person account (2017): a trans woman describes being humiliated by border police at the main international airport on returning from abroad - appearance-based controls as a daily nightmare for trans people; officers questioned her right to be in the country despite 15 years' residence.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying migration-news piece covers a report slamming this country's border waiting zones as unequal, humiliating and discriminatory.

Foreign advocacy outlet (Aug 2024): a traveller at a hostel in a large provincial city was threatened with 'transphobia' charges by the manager after raising concerns about a man in the female-dorm bathroom - a contested incident reflecting gendered-space tensions in this country. (Source has a sex-based-rights perspective.)
The national rights ombudsman: new framework decision on the rights of transgender people - official findings and guidance on discrimination against trans people in this country.

A national daily (Mar 2025): this country updates its official travel advice for a major destination after that destination moved to recognising only sex assigned at birth — travellers' documents and visa/ESTA applications must match, with advice to monitor the destination's embassy site for changes.
A cable-news report (May 2013): covers the first same-sex wedding in this country shortly after its marriage-equality law took effect.
